A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CMAT framework, and their main text, equations, tables, and retained figures support comparison. V1 ends with references; v2 adds supplementary material, but its Figures 5 and 6 contain empty boxes rather than visual results, limiting comparison of those analyses.

before.justification: V1 reports original affordance-segmentation results on PIAD, PIADv2, and LASO, along with loss, teacher, and backbone ablations in Tables 1–3.

after.justification: V2 retains original segmentation experiments and ablations in Tables 1, 2, and 4, including revised numerical results.

M1.justification: CAST becomes LAS, retaining the same feature projections, modality embeddings, token fusion, upsampling, and three pretraining objectives. However, v1 explicitly specifies an MLP reconstruction decoder, whereas v2 Table 5 specifies a four-layer decoder with six heads. The PDFs do not resolve whether this reflects an architectural change or inconsistent documentation.

E1.justification: Both versions use over 10,000 Objaverse/Behavior-1K models spanning 101 categories for pretraining and evaluate visual prompting on PIAD/PIADv2 and textual prompting on LASO. The efficiency comparison and supplementary descriptions do not establish additional dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: The segmentation comparator sets in Tables 1 and 2 remain unchanged; Baseline is relabeled Ours(w/o CMAT). V2 adds a separate efficiency comparison against IAGNet, LASO, and GREAT in Table 3, extending these existing comparators to resource evaluation.

E3.justification: V2 adds parameter-count and VRAM evaluation while retaining the stated segmentation splits, metrics, training budgets, and sampling settings. Supplementary Section 7.2 reports 378×378 rendering, conflicting with the 224×224 setting retained in both versions' main text. This does not establish which resolution was actually used or whether experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The loss, teacher, and backbone ablation designs are retained, and v2 adds a readable efficiency analysis. Supplementary Sections 8–9 describe PCA before task-specific fine-tuning and additional complex-object cases, but Figures 5–6 are empty. Whether these supply distinct analyses beyond the existing feature and segmentation visualizations cannot be verified.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or statistical error bars. V2's VRAM ranges describe resource usage rather than statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes the proposed method's PIADv2 Seen AUC from 93.59 to 93.01 and aIoU from 45.88 to 44.88. The corresponding ablation table changes reconstruction-plus-affinity aIoU from 44.50 to 44.13 and the DINOv2-teacher result from 43.70 to 43.26. Other benchmark values and principal rankings remain unchanged. V2 newly reports resource figures, including 300M parameters and 4–8 GB VRAM for its model versus GREAT's 4B and 16–30 GB.

T1.justification: V1's explicit nearest-neighbor KoLeo loss definition in Equation 5 is removed and replaced by a verbal description. V2 adds a formal visibility condition and visible-view feature-averaging definition in supplementary Equation 9. The shared affinity, pooling, and fusion mathematics remains equivalent; neither version supplies theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central claims about CMAT transferring semantic structure and achieving strong segmentation results remain. V2 narrows the segmentor's novelty claim: v1 presents CAST as a separate architectural contribution, whereas v2 describes LAS as a standard co-attentional architecture. V2 also adds an explicit accuracy-and-efficiency claim in the abstract and introduction.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations concerning deployment efficiency, semantic organization beyond better initialization, and limited benefits from increasing training data alone, although no data-scaling study is tabulated. The supplement further interprets features as learning affordance parts without task-specific fine-tuning. The existing limitation that benchmarks test only one prompt modality at a time remains.

D1.justification: V2 adds an implementation-access link and substantial supplementary specifications: architecture dimensions and heads, patch size, camera/depth handling, feature interpolation, approximately 50,000-point reconstruction, voxel radius, visibility tolerance, and feature aggregation. These materially expand reproducibility documentation without proving procedural changes. However, rendering-resolution and decoder descriptions conflict with earlier or retained specifications, and explicit reconstruction-loss details are removed.

R1.justification: The related-work categories remain, but v2 adds explicit OpenAD/OpenKD discussion and citations such as SegCloud, PartAfford, and VisionLLM v2, while removing robotics-context references such as ReKep and RAM. Positioning emphasizes efficient segmentation without large multimodal language models and reduces the segmentor's standalone novelty claim.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and substantial portions of the method and experimental discussion are rewritten. V2 removes the contribution bullet list, adds a method overview, renames CAST to LAS, renumbers stages from 1–3 to 0–2, compresses auxiliary-loss explanations, and introduces acknowledgment and supplementary sections. This is extensive narrative restructuring despite the largely retained framework.

P2.justification: V1's conceptual Figure 2 is removed; the other main illustrations are retained with renumbering, revised captions, and framework labels. V2 adds efficiency and architecture tables, relabels the model rows in Table 1, and rearranges surrounding content. Its two new supplementary figure slots are empty, so they do not supply inspectable visualizations.

improvement.justification: V2 adds useful implementation documentation, an implementation link, and resource comparisons. These benefits coexist with incomplete supplementary figures and conflicting rendering specifications. It also retains a claimed 7.85-point PIADv2 Seen advantage after Table 1 changes the relevant difference to 44.88−38.03=6.85. With the core evidence largely retained but new material introducing verification and consistency problems, a reliable net quality improvement cannot be established.
